paper_title: WebGLM Towards An Efficient Web-Enhanced Question Answering System with   Human Preferences
caption: retriever time analysis.
model_annotation: The chart illustrates a retriever time analysis by breaking total runtime into component stages across four summary points. The horizontal axis lists the categories “Avg.”, “50%”, “75%”, and “90%” in that left-to-right order, and the vertical axis is labeled “sec.” with a linear scale showing values from 0 up to roughly 9, with evenly spaced tick marks at about 2-second intervals. Each category is shown as a single stacked vertical bar whose segments correspond to the legend entries: “Search” (dark navy), “Fetch” (medium blue), “Extract” (light blue), and “Retrieval” (very light blue). For “Avg.”, the total bar height is a little above 5 seconds (≈5.3 s), composed of Search at about 1.8 s, Fetch about 2.2 s, Extract about 0.6 s, and Retrieval about 0.7 s. For “50%”, the total is around 3.5 s, with Search ≈1.2 s, Fetch ≈1.6 s, Extract ≈0.3 s, and Retrieval ≈0.4 s. For “75%”, the total is a little above 5 seconds (≈5.3 s), with Search ≈1.5 s, Fetch ≈2.3 s, Extract ≈0.6 s, and Retrieval ≈0.9 s. For “90%”, the total reaches close to 9 seconds (≈9.0 s), made up of Search ≈2.0 s, Fetch ≈4.8 s, Extract ≈0.7 s, and Retrieval ≈1.5 s. The bars are not presented as sorted by magnitude; they follow the labeled summary order, and there is no additional visual emphasis such as outlines or annotations beyond the color legend.
